items.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Miles was, he was, more or less, a genius at putting together groups that worked.

ctx.x: [chuckling] They don’t work, you know. So, you had to be humble, and, and willing to work together, in spite of having ability, and sensibilities. And Miles was, he was, more or less, a genius at putting together groups that worked.

Does uh, does having a knowledge of a person’s uh...self, for wont of a better word, does that affect or impact the way you might, say, again in the case of Ellington, write for, for individuals? You know, Ellington said, it helps, he says, “You can’t write music for someone unless you know how that person plays poker,” and, I mean, I guess you could sort of think of poker in a metaphorical sense, but have you found that to be the case? Having, obviously a knowledge of someone’s musical range, but their uh,…
